title: Anchoring Effect
source_detail: 동아(윤정미) 중2 Lesson 4 READING 본문 — Anchoring Effect
body_text: Somi: I'm looking for a lipstick for my mom. Salesperson: How about this? Somi: Expensive! I thought (that) I could buy a lipstick for 30 dollars. Salesperson: This is also popular. Somi: That's better! Hold on, Somi! Your budget is 30 dollars, but you are buying a 40-dollar lipstick. The 40-dollar lipstick sounds cheap only because the salesperson showed you a 50-dollar lipstick first. This is an example of the anchoring effect. Usually, the first piece of information becomes an “anchor” and influences the shopper’s decision. In your case, the 50-dollar lipstick was the anchor. Somi, don’t just rely on the first piece of information that is given to you.
